summary: Plantable explosives sold at Ammu-Nation and used to blow open safes and armoured truck doors.
body: PowerPyx advises buying them at Ammu-Nation before robbing Kingpin Bowling, where they destroy the office safe.
PowerPyx also describes using them on shop back-room safes and on the rear door of an armoured truck, and says some are found in the back of Yasmani's shop after his jobs.
IGN's weapons guide counts 4 explosives and its table lists them as Molotov, Sticky Bomb, Flash Grenade and Frag Grenade; its text list names only Frag Grenade and Sticky Bomb.
IGN and Game8 both write the name in the singular, Sticky Bomb.
IGN says Sticky Bombs go on sale at Ammu-Nation, under Ammo & Equipment then Explosives, for 185 dollars each after the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check, and that each character carries up to four.
IGN says Yasmani, a Chapter 3 contact, keeps a crate of them in the garage behind his office, refilled by tapping L1/LB, and that some may turn up early at Illegal Operations such as Kingpin Bowling.
IGN says one is thrown with L2/LT and R2/RT and set off with Right on the D-pad, and that tapping R1/RB while aiming a gun throws the last equipped explosive.

IGN says safes and locked doors in banks, payday loan shops and jewellery stores only open when the bomb is planted through the on-screen prompt; a thrown bomb will not open them, and a door with an alarm sets it off.

facts.availability: Ammu-Nation after the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check; free at Yasmani's

summary: A phone app that defeats keyless-entry security so high-end cars can be stolen.
body: PowerPyx says it is given automatically at the start of the Chapter 3 mission Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS and is installed on the phone rather than bought.
PC Gamer says the key cloner arrives in Chapter 3 during the mission it calls 'Steal the Zorruso for Randy'; GameSpot says Randy hands it over around the halfway point of the story.
PC Gamer says you stand by a keyless car's door, interact and pick Clone Key, using the control stick to find a sweet spot that speeds it up; GameSpot adds that no hot-wiring is needed afterwards.
Gamer Guides also names the mission Steal the Zorruso, given by Randy in Chapter 3, as the one that hands over the key cloner, and says it both opens and starts keyless cars.
The in-game Equipment entry describes it as a sketchy phone app that gets past the security on keyless cars, for stealing the most advanced cars in Leonida.

name: Parachute
summary: A hidden pack that can be opened during long falls from aircraft or buildings.
body: PowerPyx says it is sold in the Equipment section at Ammu-Nation and shares an item-wheel slot with body armor.
PowerPyx also lists a cheat that adds a parachute.
GameSpot says every Ammu-Nation sells parachutes, usually near the body armour at the back, for $250 each, and that a bought one goes straight into the loadout.
According to GameSpot, holding L1/LB and opening the Items tab shows whether one is carried, in the bottom-left slot, where it can also be set to show or hide on the character's back.

GameSpot says a free parachute lies at each of the 25 base jump spots, mostly helipads on tall Vice-Dale County towers, marked by lights and energy drink cans; doing the jump uses it up, so leaving the roof keeps it.

GameSpot's suggested jumps are the Maven Residences roof south-west of Panos Plaza, Mount Kalaga in southern Lummox County, Mainfest Canyon in north-east Kelly County, and the Crimson Palms condominiums in north Washington Beach, which it calls perhaps the tallest building in the game.
